title: The Sack of Rome, 410
objective: After this level you can explain Alaric's sack of Rome and its shock to the Roman world.
summary: In 410 CE Alaric’s Visigoths plundered Rome for three days, the first foreign capture in about 800 years. Augustine answered with The City of God.

cards.headline: In 410 CE, Rome fell to an enemy for the first time in about 800 years.
Alaric at the gates
cards.body: Stilicho, the western empire’s leading general, had held the Visigoth leader Alaric off, but he was executed in 408 CE. In 410 CE Alaric’s Visigoths sacked Rome and plundered it for three days. The Goths had been settled inside the empire since the years after Adrianople.

cards.headline: A shock to the world
cards.body: The scholar Jerome wrote that the city which had taken the whole world was itself taken. Augustine of Hippo wrote The City of God partly to answer pagans who blamed the sack on the abandonment of the old gods.

cards.fact: Rome was no longer the capital when it fell.
cards.context: By 410 CE the western emperor Honorius lived at Ravenna, a city protected by marshes, while his old capital was plundered.

cards.headline: The sack: witnessed
learned: The emperor was safe at Ravenna
Augustine wrote The City of God

questions.prompt: Why did Augustine write The City of God?

options.label: To answer pagans who blamed Christianity
To praise Alaric as a liberator
To plan new walls for the city

questions.explanation: Some pagans blamed the sack on abandoning the old gods; Augustine wrote partly to answer them.

questions.prompt: From Level 18: which people had sacked Rome in about 390 BCE?
questions.explanation: Gauls led by Brennus sacked Rome in about 390 BCE, about 800 years before Alaric.
